speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a generalized nonpruritic rash alongside a recent high fever and seizure. To narrow this down, can you tell me if you noticed any sore throat or flu-like symptoms before the fever started?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (though the fever duration and seizure are atypical, the age and rash pattern are concerning) OR Viral Exanthem with febrile seizure. Given the high fever and seizure, I must rule out bacterial meningitis or sepsis first.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C_Reactive_Protein, Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate, Blood_Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_Closer_Inspection, Neck_Spine_XRay.
